notes.made: David Pack got the chords, melody and part of the lyric in about ten minutes on 4 July 1979, at the piano in his home studio while his family packed for a trip, and put it on a reel-to-reel before they left. He worried the words were 'Hallmark-card cheesy' and phoned Michael McDonald, who told him that a Holiday Inn band playing it would be a good thing. On the record David C. Lewis plays Fender Rhodes, piano and a Prophet-5, Christopher North plays Hammond, and Ernie Watts plays the sax.
notes.context: Ambrosia started as a prog band, and fans read the album title One Eighty as a 180-degree turn. Warner Bros. put the single out in March 1980 and it went to 3 on the Hot 100 and the adult contemporary chart, number one on Radio & Records, and into the top 40 of the soul chart, which few soft rock bands managed.

listen_for.note: Lewis on Rhodes with a Prophet-5 alongside it, the polysynth that turns up all over this era.
Ernie Watts on sax. He also plays on Arthur's Theme a year later, so he bookends this era.
Four of the band sing harmony (Puerta, Jones, Drummond behind Pack), which is why it sounds like a group record rather than a singer with hired backups.

leads_to.title: You're the Only Woman (You & I)
leads_to.why: The follow-up single from One Eighty, also Pack's, which got to 13 in the summer of 1980.

notes.unverified: The panel line mentions 'the gospel lift at the end'; I found no source describing the ending, so it's left out.

culture.title: Chart peaks
culture.line: Released 19 March 1980, it reached 3 on the Hot 100 and adult contemporary, 2 on Cash Box, number one on Radio & Records, and the top 40 of the soul chart.

culture.title: Pack's remake
culture.line: David Pack recut it for his 2005 solo album The Secret of Movin' On.
